plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not lose focus when tabbing away after typing an invalid date, causing it to remain visible. This occurs because there is no blur event listener on the input field to hide the picker when focus leaves, and the picker itself is not focusable to retain focus when interacted with via keyboard.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that hides the datepicker if it is active and the active element is not the picker or input. Additionally, make the picker element focusable by setting tabindex=-1 and focusing it when shown, ensuring the blur listener can detect when focus has moved to the picker. Remove the tabindex when hiding to avoid leaving unnecessary attributes.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The datepicker will now close when tabbing away from the input field, regardless of whether the entered date is valid or invalid. This ensures that keyboard users can navigate away from the date field without the datepicker obstructing other content or interfering with screen reader navigation.
functional_risks: Adding tabindex and focus to the picker may cause unexpected focus behavior if the picker is not intended to be focusable.
The blur listener may hide the picker prematurely if the active element check fails due to timing issues.
Making the picker focusable could interfere with custom styling or assumptions about the picker's DOM structure.
verification_requirements: Verify that typing a valid date and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Verify that typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Verify that clicking on the datepicker does not cause it to close when the input loses focus.
Verify that the datepicker remains open when interacting with it via mouse or keyboard.
Verify that inline datepickers are unaffected by these changes.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not close when tabbing away from the input field because there is no blur event listener on the input to hide the picker, and the picker element is not focusable to retain focus during keyboard interaction. Additionally, the input field is not reachable via Tab because the picker's show() method focuses the picker element, removing focus from the input.
plan.repair_strategy: 1. In Picker.js, modify show() to make the picker element focusable (tabindex=-1) without focusing it, so the input retains focus. In hide(), remove the tabindex. 2. In index.html, add a blur event listener on the input field that hides the picker when focus leaves the input and the new focus is not the picker element or its children. This ensures the picker closes when tabbing away but stays open when interacting with it.

<script type="module">
import Datepicker from './js/Datepicker.js';
const form = document.getElementById('delivery-form');
window.picker = new Datepicker(document.getElementById('delivery-date'), {format: 'yyyy-mm-dd', minDate: '2024-05-01', maxDate: '2024-06-30'});
form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
  event.preventDefault();
  document.getElementById('status').textContent = 'Delivery set for ' + new FormData(form).get('delivery');
});
// Hide datepicker when tabbing away from the input field
const input = document.getElementById('delivery-date');
input.addEventListener('blur', function() {
  if (window.picker && window.picker.picker && window.picker.picker.active) {
    const pickerEl = window.picker.picker.element;
    // If focus moved to the picker or inside it, keep the picker open
    if (document.activeElement === pickerEl || pickerEl.contains(document.activeElement)) {
      return;
    }
    window.picker.hide();
  }
});
window.__ready = true;
</script>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The datepicker will now close when tabbing away from the input field, regardless of whether the entered date is valid or invalid. The input field remains in the tab order and can be reached via Tab. The picker remains open when interacting with it via mouse or keyboard because the picker element is focusable and the blur listener checks for focus within the picker.
functional_risks: The blur listener may hide the picker prematurely if the active element check fails due to timing issues (e.g., focus moves to the picker but the blur fires before focus is set).
Making the picker focusable could interfere with custom styling or assumptions about the picker's DOM structure.
Inline datepickers are unaffected because the changes only apply to non-inline pickers.
verification_requirements: Verify that typing a valid date and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Verify that typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Verify that clicking on the datepicker does not cause it to close when the input loses focus.
Verify that the datepicker remains open when interacting with it via mouse or keyboard.
Verify that inline datepickers are unaffected by these changes.
Verify that the input field is reachable via Tab from the start of the page.

<script type="module">
import Datepicker from './js/Datepicker.js';
const form = document.getElementById('delivery-form');
window.picker = new Datepicker(document.getElementById('delivery-date'), {format: 'yyyy-mm-dd', minDate: '2024-05-01', maxDate: '2024-06-30'});
form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
  event.preventDefault();
  document.getElementById('status').textContent = 'Delivery set for ' + new FormData(form).get('delivery');
});
// Hide datepicker when tabbing away from the input field
const input = document.getElementById('delivery-date');
input.addEventListener('blur', function() {
  if (window.picker && window.picker.picker && window.picker.picker.active) {
    const pickerEl = window.picker.picker.element;
    // If focus moved to the picker or inside it, keep the picker open
    if (document.activeElement === pickerEl || pickerEl.contains(document.activeElement)) {
      return;
    }
    // Process the input value to update the datepicker's selection
    window.picker.setDate(window.picker.inputField.value);
    window.picker.hide();
  }
});
window.__ready = true;
</script>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can tab away from the date field to close the datepicker regardless of date validity. The picker remains operable via mouse and keyboard without premature closure. Focus management follows native dialog behavior.
functional_risks: The blur listener may commit invalid dates if validation logic changes.
Making the picker focusable could affect custom styles or assumptions about the picker's DOM structure.
Inline datepickers are unaffected by these changes.

Verify that typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and reverts the input.
Verify that clicking on the datepicker does not cause it to close when the input loses focus.
Verify that the datepicker remains open when interacting with it via mouse or keyboard.
Verify that inline datepickers are unaffected by these changes.
Verify that the input field is reachable via Tab from the start of the page.
